celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿سَأَلَ سَائِلٌ﴾ a caller called for ﴿بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ﴾

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿لِلْكَافِرِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دَافِعٌ﴾ He is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth…" (the ayah).

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ connected to وَاقِعٍ ﴿ذِي الْمَعَارِجِ﴾ the ascending-places of the angels, namely the heavens.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿تَعْرُجُ﴾ read with tāʾ and with yāʾ ﴿الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ﴾ Gabriel ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ i.e. to the place where His command descends from the heaven ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, i.e. the punishment befalls them on the Day of Resurrection ﴿كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾ relative to the unbeliever, because of the hardships he meets in it; as for the believer, it will be lighter for him than a prescribed prayer he prays in this world, as has come in the hadith.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ this was before he was commanded to fight ﴿صَبْرًا جَمِيلًا﴾ i.e. with no anxious complaint in it.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ﴾ i.e. the punishment ﴿بَعِيدًا﴾ as not going to happen,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَنَرَاهُ قَرِيبًا﴾ as happening without any doubt.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّمَاءُ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, i.e. it befalls ﴿كَالْمُهْلِ﴾ like molten silver,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ﴾ like wool, in lightness and in flying about with the wind,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَلَا يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا﴾ a relative [does not ask about] his relative, because each is occupied with his own state.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the close relatives are made to see one another, and they recognise one another but do not speak; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ﴾ the unbeliever wishes ﴿لَوْ﴾ in the sense of أَنْ ﴿يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ﴾ with kasra on the mīm and with fatḥa ﴿بِبَنِيهِ﴾

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَفَصِيلَتِهِ﴾ his clan, [so called] because he is separated (faṣl) from it ﴿الَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ﴾ which gathers him in,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ يُنْجِيهِ﴾ that ransoming; conjoined to يَفْتَدِي.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a rejection of what he wishes. ﴿إِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. the Fire ﴿لَظَى﴾ a name for Hell, because it blazes (tatalaẓẓā), i.e. flames up against the unbelievers,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿نَزَّاعَةً لِلشَّوَى﴾ plural of شَوَاة, which is the skin of the head.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿تَدْعُوا مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّى﴾ from faith, by saying: "To me! To me!"

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَجَمَعَ﴾ wealth ﴿فَأَوْعَى﴾ held it in his container and did not pay Allah's due from it.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا﴾ an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial, ḥāl muqaddara), and its explanation is:

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿إِذَا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعًا﴾ at the time evil touches him,

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا﴾ at the time good, i.e. wealth, touches him, withholding Allah's due from it,

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ فِي أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَعْلُومٌ﴾ it is the zakat,

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿لِلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ﴾ the one who refrains from asking out of modesty and so is deprived,

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ fearful;

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍ﴾ its descent [is not safe from].

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ﴾ of slave women ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿فَمَنِ ابْتَغَى وَرَاءَ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْعَادُونَ﴾ those who overstep the lawful into the unlawful.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ﴾ — in one reading in the singular — what they have been entrusted with in matters of religion and of this world, ﴿وَعَهْدِهِمْ﴾ taken from them concerning that ﴿رَاعُونَ﴾ guardians,

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِشَهَادَتِهِمْ﴾ — in one reading in the plural [بِشَهَادَاتِهِمْ] — ﴿قَائِمُونَ﴾ they establish it and do not conceal it,

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَى صَلَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ﴾ by performing it at its times;

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ مُكْرَمُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَمَالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قِبَلَكَ﴾ towards you ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. keeping their gaze fixed,

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ﴾ of you ﴿عِزِينَ﴾ also a ḥāl, i.e. in groups, circle upon circle, saying in mockery of the believers: "If these enter Paradise, we shall surely enter it before them." Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a deterrent to them from their coveting Paradise. ﴿إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُمْ﴾ like others ﴿مِمَّا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ from sperm-drops; so Paradise is not to be coveted on that account, rather it is coveted only through piety (taqwā).

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿فَلَا﴾ the lā is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشَارِقِ وَالْمَغَارِبِ﴾ of the sun, the moon and all the stars ﴿إِنَّا لَقَادِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿عَلَى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ﴾ bring in their place ﴿خَيْرًا مِنْهُمْ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ unable to do that.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ﴾ leave them ﴿يَخُوضُوا﴾ in their falsehood ﴿وَيَلْعَبُوا﴾ in their worldly life ﴿حَتَّى يُلَاقُوا﴾ meet ﴿يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ﴾ the punishment in it,

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ﴾ the graves ﴿سِرَاعًا﴾ to the place of gathering, ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَى نَصْبٍ﴾ — in one reading [نُصُبٍ] with ḍamma on both letters — something set up, such as a marker or a banner, ﴿يُوفِضُونَ﴾ hastening,

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿خَاشِعَةً﴾ abased ﴿أَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ﴾ covers them ﴿ذِلَّةٌ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي كَانُوا يُوعَدُونَ﴾ ذَلِكَ is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate), and it means the Day of Resurrection.
